Food mediocre, service TERRIBLE. We were totally neglected. Still don't even know who our server was. Total disappointment. #NeverAgain

Great tapas spot. Service was good, food came out quick and rocked. Really really busy. I was there on a Monday and the place was jumping. 

If you don't like loud restaurants this is not your place. I was at a small table and had to lean in to hear. 

Great location to eat dinner even with the loud atmosphere.
Great lunch.  Great scene.  Great service.  Only issue was that I left smelling like smoke - I suppose that comes with the open kitchen concept?
Food was actually good. Unfortunately, service was horrible. They made us feel like we were getting in their way.

My wife and I waited 18 minutes at our table 
And never saw a sole. Very sad ! 
We've ate here before and it was wonderful.

The good : the brisk 31 minute walk to the restaurant from our hotel on the LES. Good thing thing there was no humidity tonight, oh wait ?

I absolutely enjoyed my experience here. The food was delicious, restaurant is beautiful, waitstaff attentive and overall just such a great vibe. Everything we ordered was so yummy and came out quickly. The only downside it is a bit too tight so if you don't like rubbing elbows with others then this isn't your restaurant. All in all I had such a fabulous night but I also had really great company so that may have helped as well... perfect date spot!

Mike was an outstanding server! Wonderful experience, delicious food, friendly and made great recommendations. Drinks are delicious. Food comes out fast and is all customizable and made to order. Accommodated allergies and sensitivities. Will definitely be coming back and highly suggest making reservations as they are very busy and fill up quickly!
A pleasant surprise. Excellent food and great service. Cocktails were very good too.  A bit expensive but reasonable.

Best first night in NYC I could ask for! The menu is exquisite. Everything delicious. Try the blueberry pisco, one of the best craft cocktails I've had in awhile. Nathan and his team were honest, attentive, fun, genuine, and made the whole experience even better. Don't skip dessert. I'd go back tomorrow.

I had the most tender seafood in my life at ABC Cocina. 

ABC Cocina's menu (out to the three ABC restaurants) looked the most unique, so I decided to try this one. I went for lunch!

Roundup of rating:
+1 star for beautiful interior decor
+1 star for friendly, attentive staff
+1 star for DELICIOUS, food (family style sharing)
+1 star for fairly quick service
+1 star for showing me what truly tender seafood should taste like

Here are individual reviews of my favorite dishes:
Charred Octopus - 5 STARS!!
This was THE MOST tender octopus I've ever had. The dish had a refreshing, light vinaigrette flavor with a hint of spice. The little potato chunks were fried to PERFECTION. No, this is not an exaggeration, the charred octopus dish was just perfect. Words cannot describe my experience eating it, you will have to come to ABC Cocina to give it a try!

Spring Pea Empanadas - 5 STARS!
The warm pea filling had melted cheese weaved throughout and everything was hugged by the perfectly fried, crunchy empanada dough. The filling had a little spicy kick to it which added another dimension to the various flavors in this one empanada. Again, words cannot describe how good the spring pea empanadas taste, but you must order them.

Griddled Fish Tacos - 5 STARS!
Before trying these, I didn't even know that grilled fish could be this tender. The fish melts in your mouth, the taco toppings compliment the fish well, and the shredded mint adds a cooling surprise for your taste buds. 

ABC Cocina has mastered the art of cooking seafood. I definitely recommend this restaurant - with the combination of the atmosphere, decor, and food, you will not regret coming here.

The restaurant was crowded and loud the night we went - full of energy.    Our group of 4 shared quite a few dishes.   Many of them were excellent including the Maitake Mushrooms, and the Tenderloin.   The Crispy Fish Tacos were also very good although I think grilling / warming the tortillas would be an improvement.  Service was good - lots of staff delivering plates, clearing, etc.
The atmosphere is great and poppin. The drinks were great as well. The food however has gone down in taste and presentation. I wasn't wowed by the food... thought it was ok

I understand that restaurant week in nyc is not a restaurant's favorite time of year because they aren't making the profit they usually would. That being said, it IS an opportunity for them to put their best foot forward to entice potential new customers. The other part to this is that not all of us who take advantage of the prix fix are cheap vultures. I've worked as a line cook then a chef de cuisine for 14 years. I feel knowledgeable enough to give and honest review. The food itself was delicious but the service was quite poor. I understand the server was at the end of his shift and moving slow, but you can't make a customer dining by themselves wait for 10 minutes before you clear and bring the check. The management also was unapologetic when this was brought to their attention.

This place is super cute! I like the fact that their three restaurants are connected. We went there Saturday night and didn't have to wait so long for a table. The food was flavorful and the ambiance was great. Wish our waiter was a little better. Would definitely go back!

Went there for Lunch. It was OK. Over priced. Beer was warm and full of foam. Server said it's the beer. I've been drinking beer for 45 years. Crock of Bull. Overall experience nothing to write home about.

This place truly gets 5 stars for ambience and creativity. We came on a crowded Saturday night- sat promptly at 7pm and had our drinks at the table by 7:15. The menu is fantastic and everything looks really good. We opted for the split pea guacamole.. sounds funky but is truly refreshing. The grilled maitake mushrooms and charred octopus were some of my favorite dishes. The cured salmon with yogurt dill sauce was the biggest disappointment. The salmon tasted like it was dipped in salt for a few weeks and we couldn't taste anything for a while after trying it. I think it was a bad piece but it left a bad aftertaste. If it wasn't for the salmon I would have totally up'd this review to 5 stars. The tres Leches cake was phenomenal too. Very romantic trendy spot to go out with friends or a date. I would come back again for sure to try more any-day.

I love the atmosphere and concept of the place (furniture store / restaurant). Our server was lovely and the food was great. Definitely pricey but also definitely one of my favorite tapas place:

-Maitake Mushrooms (sooo tender and flavorful, also if you love goat cheese I definitely recommend)
-Arroz con pollo (full of flavor and great portion for money)
-Fish tacos (okay definitely could skip, there were some pickled vegetables that were too overwhelming)

I'm so sad that this place didn't meet my expectation because I love latin/spanish food and tapas. I was also looking really forward to coming here also because it's Jean georges restaurant. 

I came here for my graduation brunch and I'd say everything we ordered was mediocre at best.. we got patatas bravas, gambas and croquette and everything was bland, and definitely I had better at other venders. Restaurant is beautifully decorated and pleasing to be at but that what we ordered weren't just great. Maybe I should try other food next time? Not sure yet.

It was pretty inside. I thought the food was fine but I wasn't as amazed as I thought I would be after reading good reviews over the years. We shared the guacamole, mezcal cured salmon, crispy calamari, crispy seafood rice, and short rib tacos. It was good, don't get me wrong, I just wasn't blown away by the food.

Despite the nice atmosphere and an excellent service, the food is nothing special and overpriced: almost $30 for an ok rice with chicken (why?) and $20 for a simple chips and guacamole. The mushroom with goat cheese was probably the best one. Prepare your wallet...

ABC Cocina has consistently mind blowing, mouth watering food! Every time I visit I am so pleased with the service, atmosphere, and menu. The dining room is beautiful and so cute down to the smallest detail. On my most recent visit I went during restaurant week and was impressed with the affordable price. I had the tomato salad to start and was blown away by how flavorful and complex it was. It was sweet, spicy, acidic, and salty all at the same time! Absolutely delicious!
One of the most interesting meals I've had in NYC. The charred octopus and brussels sprouts salad were two highlights but everything we ate and drank was excellent.

The food at abcCocina is exceptional but what really blew me away was the service. Four of us went for dinner for a friend's birthday and we couldn't discretely tell the waiter to bring a birthday cake, but kept mentioning his birthday when the waiter came around. Before we even thought of ordering our tab, he came over with a personal size flan cake and a candle on top. It was the most thoughtful experience. He was also very attentive to offer a 2nd round of drinks as soon we took the last sip. He was great. A good waiter definitely makes or breaks an experience. ...now only if I knew his name.
I love this place so much. The ambience of the restaurant is always so great. The food is a bit pricey and the portions are small but it's hard to complain when it is so delicious.

Atmosphere and vibe was so great!! Cocktails were amazing!! The sweet corn empanadas were DELISH and so were the ham and cheese fritters! Mushroom tacos and chicken paella were a super let down... definitely would pass! Churros were great!! Will definitely be back for drinks and apps!

Flan tasted like fish oil and I've had better tacos from a truck

Service was great though. Enjoyed the ham and cheese croquettes and the margs were on point.

Despite being a Jean-George fan, I found our lunch at ABC Cocina to be mediocre at best.  The sprawling dining room was beautiful and packed with local business people, though thankfully the staff was able to handle the demand.  The inconsistency of the food, however, was the issue.

The meal started well enough with fresh Guacamole, vibrant sungold tomato Salsa, and warm, crunchy tortillas.  The Grilled Maitake Mushrooms, on the other hand, were nothing special.  They were served with goat cheese and in a fresno pepper vinaigrette.  The tiny portion size made the dish seem more like a side than an actual appetizer.  The rollercoaster meal continued with the tender Baby Calamari, which were stuffed with smoky chorizo, a ripe tomato salad, and chunky chickpeas. The experience went downhill again with the mushy Shrimp cooked in a horribly spicy chili oil that overpowered any of the garlic flavoring that was also supposed to be included.  

Moving onto the larger plates, the Griddled Fish Tacos with aioli and a slaw of cabbage-chili pickle had no taste whatsoever.  The final dish was a Roasted Turkey Cuban and the highlight of the meal.  The huge, crispy sandwich was packed with succulent turkey, juicy ham from Flying Pigs Farm, gooey cheese, and zesty pickles.  It was funny how one heavenly sandwich could leave us with a good taste in our mouths and come close to saving the experience.  

Overall, though, we would have been better off taking our quick lunch to abcV, their vegetable-focused spot around the corner, serving surprisingly much better food.

Moody ambiance with sophisticated lighting decor around the restaurant that spans back to the next block. Guacamole was some of the best I've had in all of Manhattan and the other dishes did not disappoint. Will definitely be back for more!

One of my new favourites!
Very attentive service, amazing ambience, good food.
Must try Crispy Fish Tacos and Churros. 
Do skip Fried Chicken Tacos, very bland and not very crispy.

My only complaints would be - 
First, their Main dishes, portions are smaller (this place has tapas style dining) it felt a tiny bit overpriced. 
As we were told by our server, you should expect to order 3-4 dishes on average between 2 people. We ordered 3 and + 1 dessert. 
Churros were served as a large portion.

Second, the food almost had no salt, they give you a tiny pinch bowl with sea salt to help yourself. 

We went here on a Friday night, the place was full, however, we did not feel rushed at all during our meal by the staff. Do recommend making prior reservations.

Quick review: food is just not good. It's definitely over seasoned and over sauced. Fish isn't really fresh and the prices are total and absolute ripoff. They price tapas like full meals so be prepared to spend $100 MORE than a normal night out. It's borderline egregious. Pass on this place and save your money.

Really over priced for what you get. 
Weak drinks, inconsistent service, and ridiculously small entrees make this a never again for me. 
The food albeit tasty did not over shadow the rest of the deficiencies
So many other great choices in NYC at this price point - keep looking

Ever since my horrible experience at ABC carpet and home (see earlier review), I have been loath to try anything in the ABC family. I came here on a  whim, not by any choosing of my own, but since someone else was treating, I obliged. 

We sat in the back and there was a charcoal smokiness that permeated the area, making it difficult to enjoy the ambience while waiting. The bread basket was good, better than what I've seen on average. We got several dishes to share but none seemed particularly memorable. They were fine but they better be if two small tacos are $20!

I think JGV sells the experience, ambience, and brand rather than quality of food. At these prices, I will go to Danny Meyer's Gramercy Tavern one block up any day. 

3 stars for a Sat night.

What a solid lunch experience today. We did all the "known for" dishes, and I've now been indoctrinated to this establishment. Service is pro. Dishes on the menu look like average fare, however they are done +++100%. $19 for guacamole?!?!, but, yea, it was really good. The micro greens were spectacular, complimented the cilantro and lime. Empanadas that I can get at a food truck, three for $23?!?!  But yea, they were good too. Completely dry, not oily, super hot temp, flavors perfect, dough did its job. The raw fluke... flavors required me to close my eyes and feel the texture and taste in my mouth. The citrus oil was good enough to drink. As for the arroz con pollo, the crisp stole the show. I'm guessing they used par-cooked rice, it separated perfectly and the chicken was firm and soft in all the right places. Fantastic lunch spot, and I'll be back.

It's was less than average. I wait for the lobster more than one hour. 4 guest 4 entrées nothing in the mean time.
I wait for my lobster for about one hour. 
The fruit plate look like one made in 10 sec is a rush 390 for 4 people whitout alcool. It was very bad.

I'm OBSESSED with this place. The food is INSANELY good and the vibes and decor are very young and fun but still very classy. This place is my go to for special events and I look forward to going every single time; If you're looking for good classy tapas, don't hesitate just go to ABC Cocina and I promise you won't regret it!

Huzzah, hat trick accomplished! I finished my damn ABCs and maybe now I can say I have officially become an adult. That's how it works, right? The Jean-Georges enterprise is a behemoth in the NYC dining scene and the Flatiron trifecta is the perfect example of why it has so much staying power here. All three restaurants are beautifully designed and trendy, with menus that can appease every type of palette. I had been to ABC Kitchen and ABV prior to my Cocina visit, and my expectations for this third venture were pretty accurate. ABC Cocina is a solid, well-oiled machine. While set up slightly differently (the entire menu is tapas-style), the vibe is similar. The menu is large and wide-ranging and all plates are executed with expert precision. No one thing blew me away, but every morsel delivered to our table was respectable at the very least. I highly recommend coming here with a larger party (two is fine, but four and up is best) -- there are plenty of communal tables and with such a lengthy food menu, I think it's safe to assume you'll want to try as much as possible. A little pricy as far as tapas go, but you're also paying for the Vongerichten experience.

We came here as a party of four on a Saturday night. Packed, as expected. A big, wide open dining space -- a key feature of all ABC venues. There are a few little, semi-private nooks, but the feel is definitely communal. 

So here's the situation: double date-blind date hybrid. Bf's friend from high school and her fiancé, who we hadn't yet met. Fingers crossed that we like him (we did, phew). But we couldn't predict our opinions knowing nothing about the chap, so obviously drinks were in order. We stuck with cocktails, which I think was a good choice. The table favorite was the
Spiced Pear Daiquiri (ron zacapa rum, ancho reyes, lime, pear), which three of us ordered by the end of the night. I'm not even a rum gal, but this was a perfectly-balanced, perfectly-autumn drink. My second cocktail of the night was the Whiskey Cider (berkshire bourbon, vermouth la copa, apple cider), also quite autumnal. Not *as* good but still solid. While I can't speak to the margarita section of the menu, it was reported to be a force and worth looking at.

Cocina is the perfect spot if you're into sharing. It's great for large parties with adventurous palettes, though there's something for everyone here. The menu is long and varied -- snacks, lighter bites (raw fish/veggies), Spanish staples, a substantial taco/empanada section and some more substantial meat-forward plates. I suggest trying something from every section if appetites allow. We ordered more than what I'll review here -- there were a few plates I didn't try to due to dietary restrictions. Everything was great, zero complaints. Our table was slightly removed from the main dining space so I initially worried about being forgotten, but the service was efficient once we put our orders in. Eats, below:

Raw shaved fluke with green chili dressing, crunchy rice, herbs: A
Light and tasty, a very elegant dish with lots of subtle flavors going on but nothing to overpowering. Nice addition of the crunchy rice for texture.

Tuna tartare, chipotle aioli, chilies, chives: A
Preparation was quite similar to a beef tartare actually -- the cut of the fish and the flavor profile -- but I didn't mind! Richer than the previous dish but still on the lighter side. Served with tortilla chips. Crowd-pleaser, a safe order for sure.

Beets, shaved apples, mustard vinaigrette, marcona almonds: A
One member of our party was allergic to apples, meaning I got a second helping of this (praise!). Perhaps the dressing was a bit heavy-handed, but overall I loved this plate. Fresh, sweet and nutty, great flavors. Everything worked together and actually worked as a good palette cleanser before our meat-forward dishes started to arrive.

Shrimp with sizzling garlic, chili oil: A
How a tapas bar does shrimp and garlic says a lot about the caliber of the place. It's a simple dish, but a classic that's virtually always a staple of menus like these. Luckily for Cocina, they nailed this one. Fresh, perfectly seasoned with a bit of a kick -- as well-executed as it comes. 

Maitake mushrooms with goat cheese, fresno pepper vinaigrette: A
One of my favorites of the night. I adore maitake mushrooms and these were delicious. Safe accompaniments here (pretty much always see red pepper and goat cheese/goat cheese adjacent served with mushrooms) but it was very well-done, all seasoned nicely. 

Octopus, smoked paprika creme fraiche, guajillo vinaigrette: A
As usual, I'm picky about my octopus dishes. I wasn't necessarily enamored with this but it was very, very good. Cooked nicely (that's the priority) and seasoned nicely, grounded in earthy accompaniments that supported the protein well. Overall, very well-executed and highly recommend for octopus fiends like me.

My family of 5 celebrated my cousin's birthday here. Her, being the only local one out of the group, suggested it so that's how we've come to hear about it. Apparently, there are multiple of these ABC restaurants, each specializing in a different cuisine (vegan, new American, etc.). This one is Spanish tapas. 

Walking in, I immediately love the ambiance, and was surprised to see how large the space is. (ABC is also a furniture store next door, so that's where they get their decor from. Don't get confused when you Google Maps it.) If you've ever been to The Bazaar by Jose Andres, this place gives off similar vibes. However, the menu, although sounds delicious, is not as creative and ambitious. The price tag is pretty high too for what you get, which is the main reason why I can't give it a full 5 stars.

We shared...
- Guacamole
- Tuna Tartare
- Patatas Bravas
- Mushroom Empanadas
- Crispy Fish Tacos
- Charred Octopus
- Crispy Seafood Rice
- Churros

Honestly, I enjoyed every single dish. I have no complaints on the taste, only the portion size. The breading on the fish tacos, for example, was outstanding and memorable. But $21 for 2 tacos? Hard to justify when I can get $1 fish tacos in SoCal. The pastry and filling of the empanadas were also a standout. Cocktails were good too. Service was decent, could've been a bit more attentive. My cousin said she likes ABCV more (the vegan one), so I'd be open to trying that next.

Love the atmosphere and vibe. Small plates concept with so many delicious foods to taste and enjoy. We ordered the chips and guacamole to start. The mushroom empanadas were que rico! And the tacos delicious too. For dessert the apple crisp with lemongrass ice cream!  Out of this world...  Service was clunky and inconsistent however.

I was really excited to bring a friend from out of town here when she was visiting, but I have to say I was extremely disappointed with the service and overall experience. Our server collectively said maybe twenty words to us the entire time. She didn't introduce herself, ask if we'd dined there before or ask if we had any questions about the menu. These are stereotypical things you'd expect, especially from a restaurant this nice. She was hasty and rude. She never checked on us. She didn't refill our drinks. She was hardly present when we tried to flag her down. She did not seem to care at all.

On the positive side, the food was great. My friend had the pancakes and loved the syrup. I had the arroz con pollo which was amazing. We also shared a delicious helping of guac.

I'd like to return eventually, but need time to recover from the awful service before I even think about it. It's quite possibly the worst service I've experienced in NYC since I've lived here.

My friend and I had a nice dinner; we both ordered the fish tacos and for dessert, the cobbler.  I was underwhelmed with both, unfortunately.  The waitstaff was terrific and the ambiance was wonderful.  Very crowded, very lively, but you could still have a conversation.  I am interested in returning to try other dishes, though.

I've always been a sucker for JG! ABC Cocina however was NOT my favorite. If your looking for really good drinks and a small bite I'll suggest it, food wasn't that great but the margs (jalapeño basil is a MUST) Made up for it along with the cool decor and buzzing atmosphere.

I had a team dinner here a few weeks ago and everyone left so satisfied I had to write a review! Many of them have been to the sister restaurants next door so they knew what was in store. Due to the large dInner party size we had a prefixe dinner menu all served family style. There was about 18 of us. Although we did all fit on one table it was very tight. Unfortunately, there might be this assumption we are all tiny but we had 9 men and 9 women not all under 90lbs. It was a little tight but we made it work. 

Food was delicious! We started with guacamole and tuna tartare. Everyone was hungry so it was a great start! We moved on to octopus, chorizo, short rib and fish tacos. Eventually we tried arroz con pollo and that was the home run! Everyone still talk about it till this day. Overall food and drinks were delicious! I would plan another team dinner but perhaps with a bigger table.

The food at ABC Cocina is excellent. We order several dishes and they showed up one by one in a timely manner, tapas style. All of the dishes were delicious, our favorites being the seafood rice and home made chorizo. ABC Cocina is a very hip, happening place. I could have been a great evening if it wasn't for the service...
Our absentee waiter Michael only made guest appearances to take our order and to drop the check. The other times I had to flag him down was to ask for more drinks, then again to remind him that only two of the drinks were delivered, to bring a dessert menu, that one of the dishes were not delivered, yet still was added to the check. He never checked on us during service. He never apologized for the mistakes. Considering that our tap ranked up $380 we could expect a little more interest. We had far more attention from the busser and food runners. 
So, if you are willing to compromise superb food in exchange of terrible service, I highly recommend ABC Cocina.

Jean-George's ABC restaurants never seem to disappoint and ABC Cocina is no exception. The atmosphere is lively and it is a fun restaurant to meet up with a group of friends. We ordered the guacamole and chips and split a few of the other dishes. A standout was the beets with apples and a mustard vinaigrette. Overall, a fun atmosphere and delicious dishes made for sharing. Just know that it's always crowded and reservations are needed.

I'm a fan of all of ABC's restaurants. They use the best ingredients, they're inventive with the dishes, and the service is always attentive. Cocina takes the inventive part of that even further. I would not call this a traditional take on Spanish cuisine in any sense. Instead of trying to serve you the classic tapas dishes, they push the envelope with incorporating black truffle to the manchego. Even classic dishes like arroz con pollo they take to the next level by reincorporating the crackled skin as a garnish. Well done all around.
Delicious food and lively atmosphere.  Our party of 4 enjoyed the potatas bravas; fritters, tacos, but the arroz con pollo was the best.

I really wish half stars existed. It wasn't quite 5 star blow your mind but still a little better than 4. I was in town for the night and my group of 5 girlfriends decided on this spot for drinks and dinner. I really wish everyone would have been down for the tasting menu, but with the amount of food we got I would say we tasted the entire menu. We started with the cheese board, guacamole, truffle, empanadas and tuna tartar (yes, I said started with). Everything was delicious and actually was the perfect size for sharing for all of us. It all came out in a timely fashion, along with our drinks and the water was kept filled all night. For our entrees, 2 of us got the crispy fish tacos (myself included), one of us got the pork tacos, one had the seafood rice and one had the arroz con pollo. There were rave reviews from everyone. The crispy fish tacos were amazing, and then we ordered another entree for the table to split which was the star dish in my eyes- the octopus. Pictures were a little difficult to take due to the lighting, but it's definitely a place I would go back. Oh yeah, GET THE CHURROS FOR DESSERT!

Must have- the truffle balls, or whatever they are properly called. They were absurd. The octopus. The crispy fish tacos. The churros.

Wish I could give an extra half star. Guacamole was the best. Music was on point. Service was good. Food was inconsistent. The cheese plate was blah and the gooey ham and cheese balls were not gooey but had a strange taste. The portions are fair as it is a tapas restaurant. Nice experience.

Overrated, over-priced.  $25 for 2 tacos?  That's almost $15 a taco or $30 for 2 tacos with Tax/Tip.  Stay away!  Over-priced, what a rip off.  

Place is too loud as well, ambiance is terrible.  You can't even hear yourself.

Service is terrible.  You just see servers standing around when your water cup is empty.  

Stay away.

I decided to give ABC Cocina another shot after a very good visit to ABCV.  All of my negatives from last visit were effectively addressed with much more attentive service (e.g. drinks brought promptly, reasonable spacing between courses, offers for more drinks). Food was also very excellent as per last time although I ordered mostly differently (didn't remember I had  ordered the beets  last time but then  I tasted them and still very good).  Last time I did not get dessert but I got the horacha Sunday this time which was delicious and highly shareable. 

I'll be back but still on the look out for return of apathetic service.

I just left ABC cocina and this review is not about the food or drinks, because those were actually quite delicious. 

I am giving this place 1 star because I came here to celebrate my sisters birthday and came with a cake. I told the 2 people at the front desk about having a dessert to celebrate (including the manager, Deanna,  as well as the bartender to get the plates and forks. Never once was I told about a "plating fee," but yet when the check came we were charged $30 bucks to eat 2 slices of cake In celebration of a birthday.  We were never told about this fee, and when I explained this to Deanna it was brushed away as "policy. " 

I will not be returning here and would not recommend,  based not on the food or drinks but lack of transparency from management
Sean Michael helped us alot when we had a major issue. Will be coming back again for ABC hospitality and great ambiance.

I absolutely love this restaurant! I came here last week for the third time and it continues to live up to my expectations. The margaritas are amazing. I haven't tried their flavored margs, but the classic one is to die for. The guacamole is also awesome. I had the fish tacos and you get two in an order. For me, it was the perfect amount, but some people might want to get a side dish. The fish was perfectly fried and super flaky. We did not get dessert because we were full, but I have had their sundae before and it is one of my favorite desserts in Manhattan. Definitely a must try restaurant if you like latin/mexican food!

Side note: It is a little pricey so I would make this more of a special occasion dinner.

I've been to ABC Cocina for dinner twice now, and each time the experience was bueno. I love all the ABC chains. In fact abcV is the only completely vegetarian restaurant I'll eat at! This chain of restaurants is *chef's kiss*. 

This time around I dined with my best friend before a concert. Everyone was super accommodating and, since we were early, they allowed us to grab a drink at the bar. As soon as the drinks got there, though, they ushered us to our table. Table usherer was wearing an awesome graphic print shirt too. How funky fresh.

The bartender took the time to explain to us why a specific tequila was being used in the drink we ordered and we sent her on her merry way and trusted her. Boy was she right - damn were those spicy margaritas good! It's at a place like this that I don't even ask the bartender to give me a "skinny" version mostly because I know how fresh the ingredients must be. You feel healthy downing these margs - my only complaint? A lot of ice. Would've appreciated a bit more drink before having to order a second. But these seriously hit the spot.

The share plate method of dining has not always been my favorite, but at ABC Cocina, I don't mind it one bit. The plates are large enough to be shared by 2 people, so when you're browsing the menu, you're essentially thinking about it like "ok, this is an app for 2." The waiters always tell you just as much as you should order. They let you know if you'll be hungry or if you should perhaps order one more dish.

I'd go hungry to this place and make sure you're in the mood to socialize. You'll always feel relaxed here.

Only reason this review is missing the 5th star is because, say it with me people, "Sarah doesn't give 5 stars!!!!!‍.... unless it's like, the best steakhouse I've ever eaten at in my life."

Came in here on 3/2 around 5:30 with my friend trying to get a drink. Was super excited to try out their food since it looked so great but the bartenders failed to even hand us a food menu. Even receiving the drink menu took a few minutes when the bar was very slow. They also did not ask us if we wanted another drink. The party next to us got food menus, drinks and they checked if everything was okay as well.

ordered take out from here and for $65 I would rather have ordered a pizza thats how bad it was. I loved this place and AbcV pre Covid but this was god awful and felt like it was saved and not cooked fresh. Also I hear not all the same chefs are there. Drove 20mins to pick up $65 worth of food that I threw in the garbage. Go somewhere else.

I'm so glad this place is allowed to operate during Covid with outside seating. We had the reservation for 8:30p and arrived a few minutes late. The hostess was quite unpleasant. First, she claimed we had not made a reservation and then was quick to state that we should order everything right away because the kitchen is closing soon. Not the best start but it was all erased by the absolutely A.M.A.Z.I.N.G waiter we got. He right away put us at ease and said there was absolutely no rush to order. His service was top notch throughout the dinner and it just made the food taste even better. The guacamole with their signature tomato salsa is a great way to start. Their salsa is so good that I ordered more separately as well. They offer cold pressed juices for folks like me who don't drink alcohol. I ordered their "Green Glow - spinach, kale, green apple, citrus" and it was extremely refreshing. The entrees were very fresh. You HAVE to try their sweet corn pudding (only available for patio dining) with blueberries and cornmeal shortbread to finish off the meal. The BEST sweet corn pudding I've ever had. The waiter was very attentive without being overbearing. Overall, an excellent experience and will be back for sure. The less star is because of the hostess who such a contrast to our waiter.

Jean-Georges Vongerichte's ultra chic Latin American fusion restaurant was our brunch pick couple of months ago - way before COVID. I am late in reviewing this place but it truly deserves 5 stars! The ambiance is great here to make it a date night spot or just a casual meal with friends. Small plates so the bill adds up quickly but everything we ordered was on point. Friendly tip, make reservations because it's hard to get a table on the weekend.
Highly underwhelming. The food is very highly priced and the taste just doesn't match the price point. I've been to ABC kitchen before which I loved but ABC Cocina is a waste of money.

-guacamole. Very fresh. Great presentation. Homemade chips with it are the perfect amount of crispy.
-drinks: grape concord mimosa is delicious. I found it a little odd to see a mimosa on a dinner menu but it was absolutely delicious. I got two.
The mock tail was perfect for my partner.
-the hopper shrimp: very good with a squeeze of lemon 
-chicken tacos: had a great spicy kick to Them. The chicken tasted delicious. Highly recommend 
-flounder fish tacos: the whole thing tastes very fresh. There's a lightness to it a even though it's fried. The fish is a big piece which you don't get often when ordering tacos. Highly recommend
Aesthetics wise from the atmosphere to the serving of dishes, everything was perfect. we had a wonderful date night and will be back again.

Came here a couple of months ago when NYC was still doing indoor dining, and they took very good precautions to make sure their guests felt safe. Everything we ordered was SO good, and the service was fast and friendly. Two of my favorites were the arroz con pollo and the octopus. Will definitely be going back!
Great restaurant.  Unique both food and ambiance, great date spot, some interesting wines such as Carmenere. Affordable considering Jean Georges

Was here for a celebratory meal but had a horrible and utterly unacceptable experience.  The General Manager, Dana Fortunato-Lawrie, was long on excuses and short on remedies.  She knew the "right" things to say, but when it came to expressing genuine concern for her guests, she really struggled.  The only staff members with a can-do attitude were the bussers.

Our waiter, a blue-haired individual, was rude and totally incompetent.  We ordered two alcoholic pitchers ($72 each!) and he tried to upsell us when we weren't even through drinking what we had.  Transparently exploitative and incongruous with the Jean-Georges image.  We were never checked in on and during our time at the restaurant we saw at least 2 tables leave in a huff.  Our waters and beverages were never topped up, and we were rushed into ordering more food than we wanted. 

With everything going on in the world, this is not the time to be slacking.  It is unfathomable that anyone, much less frequent Jean-Georges diners like us, was treated with such condescension and disdain.

We ordered the guacamole ($19); squash empanadas ($15 for two pieces); black truffle, fontina, and farm egg pizza ($26); roasted cauliflower ($27); ramen ($27).  The pizza was the best item we had; the other items were passable.  The ramen was totally inedible, forget "broth," it was chili oil and water.  Disgusting.  Its only saving grace was the tiny portion.  Truly repulsive.

One of my friends actually cried at the dinner table because we were subjected to racism and transphobia.  Our treatment was appalling by any standard, but all GM Dana saw fit to do was bring out 2 mini-cupcakes and some churros ($15).  It was disrespectful and a slap in the face.  

Overall, a truly humiliating experience that no one should ever be subjected to.

DEFINITELY NOT RECOMMENDED.

Good spot for a chic but casual Latin-inspired brunch. 

My friend and I split the crudo, mushroom tacos, and fish tacos. The crudo was fresh and citrusy. The mushroom tacos were super flavorful. And the fish tacos were nicely crispy. The price point is a little high- the tacos came in a set of two for $21. Brunch came out to $40/each at the end. We came here last minute and we're glad we did!

After almost a year between visits due to Covid, we finally returned for Brunch this past weekend. Happily, nothing has changed!! The food, service and cocktails are as amazing as before! Don't miss it!

I found the food to be horrible- very acidic/ salty/over seasoned, overly complicated and overpriced. I ended up eating only a few bites of everything. My hot lemon water was the best thing I ordered. Second best was the salad with strawberries and manchego. The rest I took a few bites and tossed out. 

Service was like eating at a cafeteria....ambience was mediocre at best. Will not be dining at any of the ABC restaurants in the future. There are far too many gems in the city.
Never disappoints! Their spring pea guacamole is incredible. Tacos are great, and drinks are good too! Love Jean Georges' restaurants!!

Five stars for the food,  staff and vibe of the place.  Really considered a four star with the long wait between the delivery of tapas plates.  Dining room wasn't anywhere near full capacity. May have just been understaffed at the time. Will give it a five and the benefit of the doubt that it's not always slow on delivery. They turned it around toward the end.

I have traveled the world and eaten at many fancy restaurants however, this was the worst experience I have ever sustained. Went for a preset birthday dinner, the menu we were given had much tapas on it and a few "entrees", followed by margaritas. When we sat down we asked if we pick what we want and if we pick one of the three margarita flavors for drinks. The waitress then said, "you receive everything that is on this menu." The food came it was portion servings for 1 person for about 4 people. It was not tasty and the bill came and was more than twice the price of what we were quoted for the party reservation. Most of the party did not eat the food and the drinks (in which we asked for confirmation) were not included in the price but instead $70 a pitcher and we had about 5. Communication was terrible, staff was uneducated on their role and establishment. Overall horrible experience and disappointment.
Awesome cocktails & food. The crab cakes were very good, as was the guacamole. Definitely recommend coming through!

The portions are a little small but the food is solid. Also really liked the interior and the open kitchen.

I loved the grapefruit margarita, calamari (the breading was quite good and better than most), chipotle chicken tacos, and the arroz con pollo (the chicken was so juicy and delicious). We also ordered the pea guacamole (good but a crazy tiny portion), fluke crudo (average; I would skip), and the sirloin of beef (I would skip this one also; we ordered it medium rare but it came out more on the medium side).

For dessert, we got the strawberry rhubarb cobbler with buttermilk ice cream and the churros, both of which were also good.

Overrated garbage. They need to strip the chef of his Star. Tacos were HORRIBLE. Chicken rice was HORRIBLE and mushy. The only good thing was the shrimp and that was nothing special. Spent over $200 and was the most expensive and by far the most disgusting food we had visiting the city.

I do not recommend this place. Portion size is extremely small. Wait staff is slow.  Food came out fast flavors were amazing. Had mushroom tacos. The taco was crumbling apart and poorly executed. A little bland. The fish tacos should be called fish flavored tacos. It was all breading slaw and sauce no fish. Tasted great just extremely disappointed on the execution of such an eloquent fish. The fish had all batter and should have been cooked longer it was not as crispy as it should have been. Seemed sloppily made. The potatoes were delicious although I could fit the entire portion of the potatoes in my hand. The rosemary aioli and guajillo sauce was awesome sauce. Definitely recommend trying the habanero hot sauce if you choose to come here. Certain dishes for example all the bread dishes like French toast and churros they were generous with. Octopus is a must try and super tender and succulent. Will not be going back if you go try the octopus. Only tip for me.  
Don't go super hungry because you will leave hungry! Portion sizes are smaller than normal places for the quality of food

So delicious
When you sit outdoors you can order from the adjacent Jean G restaurant. Must try the pizza!
Food was good. Service was friendly. Was a fan of their french toast. We tried their trio of tacos, they weren't bad but needed a little bit more seasoning. The drinks were good.

I stopped by here for dinner with a colleague, and we had a great meal. It is tapas style -- we particularly enjoyed the Arroz Con Pollo and the calamari. Our server was friendly. It is a bit loud but is great for conversation with a small party (2-4).

Great food, but I would wait until they are able to staff the restaurant better.  We waited 45 minutes and had 3 dishes brought all at once, which degraded the overall experience and our ability to enjoy each one on its own.  We had an apologetic waiter, but for the amount spent, it's not worth the trouble.

I have been wanting to try ABC Kitchen for quite some time now. I made a reservation at ABC Cocina outside in order to do the "taste of all three" menus. I called the restaurant at 6pm to change my 7:15pm reservation to 7:30pm. When my fiancé and I arrived at 7:39pm on our 3 year anniversary and we were told that our table was given away and the reservation was at 7:15pm with a 15 minute grace period. Mind you there were available tables outside. I will not be coming back.

Another restaurant popularized by Kim K. 

This place does have some tasty dishes. I personally love the fish tacos and their churros. Their guacamole is also quite tasty. 

Great place for a quick bite after work!

Went for cocktails and tapas with a friend a few weeks back. We met around 5 on a weekday, and the restaurant was mostly empty. Apparently in pre-covid era it was impossible to get a reservation, but we had no trouble making one just a few hours before we arrived. 

Really, really good cocktails. Friendly and professional service. Food was good too, though we only tried a few appetizers. The pea guacamole was great, as were fish tacos. 

Nice atmosphere in the dining room, as well. And hey, if you want to buy a couch or some carpet, you can just walk upstairs to the ABC Carpet.

Got the spring pea empanadas, mushroom tacos,  squash blossom quesadillas, and sorbet. The mushroom tacos were the only thing I would have put in the "good but not amazing" category. The fact that the greens sat on top of the mushrooms meant you got a bite of either mushrooms or bitter greens. I probably would've liked it a lot more if they were more mixed. Everything else was DELICIOUS! Would totally go back

The interior is beautiful and outdoor place is quite safe/distant. Went for a brunch (reservation on resy). We got frozen drinks m (sangria base) so it's fruity, great for summer days. Food wise, relatively vegetarians friendly with options marked.

I've always wanted to try an abc restaurant before and finally tried abc Cocina. I was a little nervous because of the recent mixed reviews, but we had an amazing meal here! 

I had the frozen strawberry hibiscus sangria which was a great drink to accompany the meal. Very refreshing. 

These are the dishes we tried--

table snacks:
guacamole (5)

light & bright:
long island fluke crudo (5)

golden & crispy:
patatas bravas (4)
hopper shrimp (3)

masa & tortillas:
pea empanada (4)
mushroom taco (4)

grilled & roasted:
maitake mushrooms (5)
charred octopus (5)
sirloin steak (4)

rice & grains:
arroz con pollo (5)

The guacamole, charred octopus, and arroz con pollo were my favorite dishes! Also really liked the fluke and mushroom dishes. 

I liked that the dishes were a mix of different cuisines and the service was amazing too! I really liked the ambiance and it was casual but classy. 

Overall, a great meal at abc Cocina!

Exceptional experience! 
The restaurants ambiance is everything you expect with a Jean George experience. Dim, Sexy, elegant, delicious. A true experience. Maria gave us amazing service and we felt very welcomed. Dana the manager came by to make sure everything was great and she made sure we felt like we were a true VIP customer as they make EVERY customer feel. Thank you. Can't wait to experience more Jean George experiences.

Eh save your money, especially if your coming to New York from out of town. The service and staff are horrible and the food is nothing special. I am getting more and more disappointed with Jean Georges chain with each place I try. I should know better by now.

This was my first time visiting an ABC restaurant and I really enjoyed my experience. I like how all three restaurants and the home store are all connected to each other - at first I thought it was strange having a furniture store and restaurants under the same umbrella, but it kind of makes sense once you see the interior decor of each ABC.

The menu is pretty small but some favorites were the corn empanadas, the maitake mushrooms, and the melons with dipping sauce. I've never had anything like the melons before but I really liked how refreshing they were, with the perfect amount of bite from the spice. The corn empanadas were a dark horse and paired super well with the corn margarita, which was also a concoction I've never tried before. They had some other interesting margarita flavors as well, like ginger and spiced plum.

Overall I thought it was a very neat concept with interesting takes on Mexican / Spanish classics. Interested to see how the other two ABCs differ in cuisine.

PS - they say on the menu that the pitchers serve 5, but we got 3 between 3 people... oops?

I've been going to ABC Cocina for a while now (as well as ABC Kitchen, Nougatine and Jean Georges). I always enjoyed the fresh food and helpful service. Until now. My last visit was an utter disappointment. It took 20 minutes to have someone fill our water glasses, despite multiple efforts to flag someone down. The appetizer of melon coulis was an uninspired three wedges of un-ripened cantaloupe and honey dew. There was no taste to the melons. We mentioned this to the waiter, who just shrugged his shoulders. The fish tacos fell apart at first bite. 

Any self respecting chef or sous chef who pride themselves on farm fresh produce would not serve un-ripened melon. They would take it off the menu. We were told that it was end of season, so the melons were not ripened. 

The next day, I went to Trader Joe's (not known for the ripest produce), and found the sweetest Italian cantaloupe I've had in ages. Shame on Jean-George. Truly. I would be ashamed to serve sub-par food in such a restaurant known for quality of food and service. 

Now you're known for the money grab of serving bland, barely passable food at insane prices. I'll never return to a Jean-Georges restaurant again.

Super super good food! Such a wide array of food and all of them were great. 

Loved the Patatas Bravas

Went in on a whim with a friend and found an exquisite culinary experience with chocolate dipped churros to die for. Our server, Latricia, was incredible in helping us select the best dining experience for our tastes. Can't wait to go back!

Absolutely blown away by the amazing food and the even better service. Such a pleasure to eat at a restaurant like this. All the staff were very attentive and friendly. The management was wonderful as well too! Definitely coming back to enjoy another meal here:)

I recently went to ABC for a work dinner and oh my they delivered. The table was setup so nice with pre fixed menus printed and our company name on the top. Everyone was so kind and attentive. Didnt let our water glass stay empty for a single second. There were a lot of dishes and i dont remember the name and my fav. was all the salads, ravioli and chicken. I will be returning with my family.

ABC Cocina, part of Jean-Georges' restaurant triumvirate (Kitchen and V are the other two) in ABC Carpet & Home. It is safe to say that the three restaurants are now far more successful than the store. ABC Cocina is Jean-Georges' pan Latin American restaurant where he uses locally sourced seasonal ingredients. The cuisine is inspired by traditional LatAm dishes rather than actually being food you would expect to find in south of the Rio Grande. Having said that, the food is delicious and inventive. The cocktails are creative and go down easily. As at any Jean-Georges restaurant, the service is excellent. This was our first time back since the Pandemic and ABC Cocina is as great as it was when it first opened.

A friend and I had a impromptu thanksgiving dinner here, food was great, we had guac and chips as a starter, a few small tapas and then their thanksgiving plate with turkey, mash, chicken and stuffing and of course a few margaritas.

It took about 10-15 mins to initially get water and menus but after that the service was on point.

I would definitely recommend them and will be going back,

Such a comedown. Used to be so reliably great. Now the service is really suffering. Arrived on time for 12:30 reservation. Took a while for the server to approach. She was lovely but clearly overwhelmed (not her fault). My friend's entree arrived before our app; mine was MIA. Had to chase the server after 20 minutes asking about the whereabouts of the app and my entree. Asked for a fresh dish for my friend--later learned her eggs Benedict had an extra $25 charge for a few pieces of ham. I was asked if I wanted a fried egg with my arroz con pollo--also a $25 upcharge (!) with no mention of this beforehand. No comp for drinks or anything after the kitchen delays and service mishaps. Food is still good but disappointing experience, especially compared with pre-pandemic trips.

Overall disappointing and definitely not worth the price. I had been here a few years ago and really enjoyed it so it was a shame to see how far it has fallen. 

Pros: decor is lovely, drinks tasted good, and the guac with the hot sauce that is left on the table was good, along with the roasted tomato salsa that comes with the guac

Cons: everything else we had was relatively bland, had a very one-note flavor, and often times felt lacking in acid. We had the shrimp (perfectly cooked but bland. The runner who dropped the item at the table even said beware of spice but I could not find any heat); calamari (again the protein was well cooked but overall bland; squash empanadas (well fried and was not greasy at all but lacked flavor and needed salt); chicken tacos (chicken was cooked well and the salsa was good but it felt like it was missing a component. Maybe a slaw?) 

I also generally think the portions were VERY small for the price tag. 

The other major con was the waitstaff. Our server took over 20 min to take our order then basically disappeared the entire meal - never came back to even ask if we wanted more drinks until we were literally done with our entire meal. The food runners who brought out the dishes were efficient but basically just said what the dish was and ran away with asking if we needed anything else (like a new drink or water).

I would definitely skip and instead get tapas at Boqueria.

Had Thanksgiving dinner and it was a good choice that night. The server was pleasant and my family loved the food. I was seated towards another side of the restaurant which was more casual and noticed on my way to the ladies room there was another section more formal. I'd like to come back and try more on their menu esp on the formal dining area. Would recommend this to friends, family & coworkers to try if ever in the area.

I've tried ABC Kitchen and abcV, so finally get to try ABC Cocina which is part of Jean-George's restaurant. ABC Cocina is mixed with Latin and American flavors and its tapas-style. Loved the atmosphere and the food was so spot on. 

What I ordered: 
- Guacamole with roasted tomato salsa and warm crunchy tortillas
- Shrimp with sizzling garlic, chili oil
- Mushroom Empanadas with green chili mayo
- Spiced Ground Beef and Celery Root Empanadas
- Charred Octopus smoked paprika creme fraiche, guajillo vinaigrette
- Arroz con Pollo crackling skin, lemon zest
The best margaritas I've ever had - great atmosphere - great staff - amazing food - doesn't get any better than this

Food is amazing. It has a tapas concept. For two people I  recommend to choose 4-6 dishes. Empanadas and octopus were beyond any expectations! 
But service is far away from great. Our server during the entire time we spent there came 3 times : ask what we gonna to drink , ask what we order to eat and brought the check. I made a comment saying that plates were not changed AT ALL , had to chase other waiters to order drinks and I would like to see the dessert menu. His response was " I thought other waiters took care of you". Indeed they did but we had to catch their attention. So service really ruined my experience. But need to highlight again that food and cocktails were delicious! 
.

I came here for a Friday dinner with a friend and had a nice time! 

The ambience when you walk in is quite nice--very chic with flowers at each table. It is a popular and crowded restaurant so the tables are positioned a little closer together. If you've been avoiding crowds and people because of COVID, I would maybe re-consider indoor dining here. 

We order a couple of cocktails--I got the lavender negroni and also the grapefruit margarita. Both of which I enjoyed! The negroni was interesting, very boozy (which I loved), not too sweet with the lavender note coming in sorta like an aftertaste. The grapefruit margarita was very refreshing and light.

We also ordered the arugula salad with brussel sprouts and cheese. It was mixed with a tangy vinegrette that was also very tasty. 

For our entrees, we each ordered our own tacos. I got the flounder tacos which came out just fried and was very hot and crispy. The tacos were delicious! Each order comes with two sizable tacos--I had huge pieces of fish on each of my tacos. Super delicious and definitely hit the spot.

We also ordered dessert. We ordered the cocoa tres leches cake, which came with a scoop of delicious ice cream and a thin piece of caramelized banana. It had pieces of brownie sprinkled on top which also complimented the dessert dish very well. 

I would definitely come here again! The restaurant is a bit on the pricer side but I think well worth a date night or just a nice evening out.

Great margaritas!! Their habanero margarita might be the spiciest I've ever had.

The food was also good, but the drinks were memorable.

Good food. Good service.
Missing 1 star because for some reason, the restaurant is SO COLD despite the doors being closed. I know, I went in the middle of winter, but no heating... really??

Nice, Vegan friendly place with an eclectic menu that delivers on variety and taste. This will satisfy any palate looking for delicious Latin inspired dishes. It's a modern take on Latin favorites. 

Can't stress enough what a tasty meal we had. 

Dishes are served tapas style in smaller portions and meant to be shared. With a Vegan at our table, we ordered a mix of stuff including, the arugula salad, guacamole and chips, calamari, French toast, mushroom tacos, flounder tacos, eggs Benedict, and the Beef empanadas. Every dish was simply delicious. Our two top choices were the empanadas and the crispy calamari. Both were perfectly cooked and bursting with delicious flavors. 

Service was impeccable and extra kudos for being open during the Blizzard Bomb. 

Very highly recommended!
Cute little spot in the city. The food was good and loved the ambiance here. It felt upscale with some nice comfort food with a slight spin. Check it out!

Some good things, some mediocre. At end of today probably not worth price... 
Good: shrimp ajillo, mushroom empanadas, brussel arugula salad (although a bit plain), pastatas bravas, shishitos 
Mediocre: fish tacos and chipotle chicken tacos (fried chicken and no chipotle flavor!)
Fine: quesadilla (decent but bland)

I came here solo after a workout around the block on a Saturday around 1:30pm. The bar had a few seats occupied, but plenty open seats at the time. I  got the Huevos Racheros and Grapefruit Margarita (yes, after a workout - it was a Saturday, live a little). I loved the portion size, it was just right - unlike massive US portions. If you are a big eater, might leave hungry - but was just right for me. Both the bartenders were super friendly and it just was a nice casual meal by myself. I would definitely come back here!

The food was delicious. There's nothing else but to say that it was delicious. The wife and I tried their arugula salad, the patatas bravas, the fried calamari, the crispy flounder tacos, the chicken tacos and the pork tacos.  For dessert we had the cocoa tres leches cake. And all was just delicious. Each bite just bring you joy. You're anxious for the next dish to come out and see how it'll surprise you. It makes the wait almost eternal. I would definitely recommend this place.

This place was perfect for an intimate conversation between friends snd the delicious food served as s catalyst for rich conversation. Everything was spot on. Empanadas, arroz con pollo,  octopus were all delicious!  The price was a tad high.

Awesome food and good service! Def worth trying along with the other ABC restaurants - Kitchen and V! One thing I would mention is that it is very loud inside but their outdoor seating is great - spread out and have heaters!

The food was atrocious, the service staff overbilled for food for one extra person that didn't come. We were treated very poorly. Staff service is slow. For Spanish food we highly recommend baby brasa!
Rude and weak  hostess with fake smiling . And the Tables are dusty . She don't even care re-clean again or change our table . Slow service definitely

This restaurant was decent! TL;DR is some of the dishes were great, however for the price I don't think it's worth it. 

The ambiance and vibe of the place is nice and clean. The staff were nice and helpful with the menu.

Came here with a large group and ordered a lot of tapas. Some were excellent (calamari was the best, fish taco was also great), however others were okay (ceviche and octopus). 

But what got me was the price. $20 for 2 fish tacos? Would I really $10 for one of those tacos? I don't think so...

Overall, glad I came once, but probably won't come again. Except for that calamari dish, perhaps :)

Really good tapas for a high end budget, and excellent service.  Sat at the bar and we asked the bartender what he recommended.  We got the fish tacos and the potatoes bravas, both were so delectable and salty!  They came out in less than 5 minutes, too.  The tab was $40 for those 2 apps, but it was worth it.
Solid with family style small plates. Like ABC Kitchen, fun industrial vibe. Good mixed drinks though the check adds up with the small plates

Restaurant was average/good. Nothing to write home about. If I was passing it on the street and they had availability I would def go. Wouldn't really go much more out of my than that to eat here. Patatas bravas and chicken tacos were best dishes we ate!

Our waiter Victor was so nice tho!!!

I had been here many years ago and I am glad to say my experience was as good as I remembered! We had some great margaritas to start off - ginger was my favorite. The plates are meant to be shared and they recommend 2-3 items per person so we got a total of 6 items for 3 people and we left VERY satisfied. 
Guacamole was very fresh and flavorful, really appreciated the fresh tortillas. The octopus was nicely cooked, I really liked the sauce and the potatoes that came with it. Hopper shrimp was good - nothing special but I love shrimp in any form.  The maitake mushrooms were a great addition, they  were meaty and had this great sauce + goat cheese - yum!
The tacos were our favorite part of the meal, we loved both fish and chicken options. Our server was super nice and so were the hosts. Overall amazing experience!

Came here for an anniversary brunch! Inside is a great atmosphere and highly recommend

Ordered the spring pea empananadas and patatas bravas for apps. Portion sizes pretty small considering the price! The waiter told us that taco orders now came with two, and on old pictures clearly can see 3 so maybe inflation problems! Apps were underwhelming, definitely wouldnt order again.

Huevis rancheros were decent, but seemed very lazy and no effort into putting it together. French toast wasnt anything special either. The entire time i was thinking "damn these are good profit margins!" 

Conchas were very good! They added a nice touch (giving it another star) for the anniversary by giving two cupcakes with candles (they looked and tasted like they were from Baked by Melissa lol) 

Overall, may just come back for dinner and try it out!

My favorite restaurant in the city. The mushroom tacos have consistently been my favorite dish in all of NYC. If you like spicy, the Diablo margarita is to die for. I highly recommend the octopus, heart of palm salad with avocado and cherries, and Long Island fluke crudo. I would skip the quail and the bbq pork tacos. They're fine, but they don't hold up to the rest of the dishes.
Delicious! Our group enjoyed multiple plates, but my favorites were the beef empanadas and arroz con pollo with chicken skin.

A lot to say about this establishment and it's all mostly positive. The restaurant is located adjacent to its sister restaurant that is all vegetarian and if you sit outside, there is a menu available that combines dishes from both establishments.

The vibe is quintessential downtown New York City with a busy side street and fancy decorations both inside and out. There is an amazing cocktail menu with fanciful combinations including a blueberry flavored whiskey sour. The taste is amazing and well crafted, expected for its pricing and geographical location of course.

For food, we ordered a bunch of vegetarian dishes and felt like kings sitting on the streets of New York with a European style atmosphere. Their best dish is a cauliflower one: whole roasted cauliflower, turmeric tahini, za'atar, pomegranate, red zhug, fresh herbs, and pistachio!

Also order the Green chickpea hummus, mint, ancient emmer pita and crudité. These two dishes alone demonstrate the shear power of some pretty killer vegetarian combinations. You won't be disappointed. 4 stars, and not 5 stars, due to its relatively small sample sizes and relatively high prices.

Nice dining spot for eating outside on a weeknight. Diverse choices to satisfy everyone. Small plates to share. One benefit of eating outside is that you are permitted to choose from not only the main ABC Cocina menu but also the menu for the sister restaurants next door (ABC Kitchen and the vegan ABCv). Lots of choices! Service is friendly and attentive. Prices seem reasonable but many small plates can add up!
Came here on a whim and truly enjoyed the corn empanada. The flavors were just so unexpected in a great way. We also had fantastic drinks!!! The watermelon and tonic is a must try.

Incredibly disappointing experience. The food was overpriced, small, and underwhelming. The tacos as Los Tacos No 1 are better and you get more. The zucchini flower quesadillas was okay, somewhat bland. The children tacos were deep fried and all I tasted was fry. The worst part of the evening is we had originally booked for outdoors. Being it was so hot the host asked us if we wanted inside instead. I asked does the menu change if we move and he told us it does limit us to be inside. I then said it's so hot we should probably go inside for the AC. After being seated all 4 guests in my party are sweating horribly. I go back to the host and ask if they can turn up the AC because it felt like outside except without a breeze. He then tells me it is because their AC has been BROKEN ALL DAY! 

It was absolutely MISERABLE. No AC in a 90 degree day, when we left the restaurant the outside was just as warm as the inside. We were all miffed about sitting inside for "AC" and a smaller menu when there was no AC. We ended up not even eating most of the food because it was too hot and the food was not that good. The waiter tried to push more dishes on us too.

While I've loved every Jean Georges restaurant I've been to, and his son's restaurants, this is the first I will not return to.

I came here for dinner and loved it!  The restaurant is quite big and has an outdoor patio in the back.  I really liked the decorations and vibe of the place.  I ordered the ginger margarita which was light on the alcohol but good with the ginger flavor.  There were two of us so we ordered 5 dishes since it was tapas style.  We basically got one dish in each category except for the rice and grains one.  First, we started with the potatoes bravas which were crispy.  I loved that there was a habanero sauce on our table when we sat down which went well with all the dishes.  Second, we got the heart of palm salad which I loved.  It wasn't really a salad per se, more deconstructed, but the heart of palm plus avocado plus the chili vinegaraitte was a perfect pairing.  Third, we got the shrimp which was my favorite dish of the night.  The shrimp literally exploded with flavor.  Fourth, we got the chicken tacos.  The chicken was breaded and the tortilla was stuffed.  As far as flavor goes, it wasn't as good as the other dishes but the habanero sauce went well with it. Finally, we got the charred octopus which came with the same sauce as the potatoes.  Would definitely come back here.

ABC Cocina is a Latin small plates restaurant in Gramercy, part of the ABC collection of stores and restaurants. I typically do not do tapas/small plates restaurants because the bill is always huge, but this was the choice of the group. We ordered two rounds of margaritas (fav was the passion fruit) and a mix plates from each section of the menu. The highlights for me were the fish tacos and arroz con pollo as they were the most substantial. I'd definitely pass on the shrimp ($20 for 5 little shrimp that did not taste fresh) and empanadas ($20 for 2 beef empanadas...). Desserts were good, especially the churros. The meal was over $100 per person and ultimately I do not think worth the price, but I did have a good time and liked most of the food. Not a place I would return to, but if you have the pockets for it, you should enjoy it.

A great tapas type place.  We ordered 5 different small plates for two of us with two bottles of water.  Total price (without gratuity) came to about $190.00 - not bad.

Good flavor, unique recipes and good service.

From Nov 3 2022 - We were originally going to go to Bocca Cucina but ended up coming here instead as the bar scene was rather dead at Bocca. There is no signage for abc on E. 19th street but we found it quite enchanting and decided to go in. We sat at the bar which had a great bar scene Inc organic cocktails and small bites. Definitely would recommend checking it out if you've never been to abc Kitchen(s) restaurants. http://www.abckitchens.nyc
Super tasty! The service is super good. My favorite dishes are Chicken noodles soup with lime, chicken rice and steak.

Great time here! Our server, I think named David I can't fully remember, but he was really really great! He gave us a lot of great advice on the menu and didn't steer us wrong once! We had the fish tacos which were my favorite, we also had the guacamole with good hot chips, the raw fish app which was also great, and the spicy sizzling shrimp which def had a kick but not too much for me, could be too much if you aren't good with spice. The ambience is also 10/10 really great experience overall
Tasted good and had rlly fun vibes but i got food poisoning after. Was so sick. Good spot for drinks at the bar only

I had high expectations going in and some were met, but others were a bit lackluster. Everything is tapas style and they recommend 6-9 for 3. The ambiance is chic and almost as whimsical as kitchen.  

Drinks: kiwi margarita- interesting flavor combos with kiwi chunks- not as tart as I'd like; ginger margarita and Meyer lemon collins were good, however, very light alcohol for all. 

Food: we ordered ham & cheese fritters, broccoli rabe quesadilla, fish tacos, sizzling shrimp, and arroz con pollo. My absolute favorite thing was the verde sauce that came on the side; the shrimp was a great portion size and loved the charred garlic and chili oil. Pass on the arroz con pollo- the crackling skin was fun but overall flavor wasn't there; broccoli rabe quesadilla- one tortilla folded in half with broccoli rabe, cheese and a sauce- uncut and not worth it. 

Service: recommendations were off; disappeared for long periods of time

Service was great, but otherwise there's no return to go back here... the food is super mediocre, especially considering the price and the fact that this is a Michelin chef's restaurant! Ambiance was also nothing special.
You can get MUCH better food for this price in New York (or for a lower price).

Came here with friends for winter 2023 restaurant week. The ambiance is amazing- high ceilings, incredible decor, open kitchen. Truly a beautiful dining experience. The restaurant week menu was $60 for 2 dishes and a dessert. Our party of 4 also ordered 3 small plates a la carte. I left very full.

But generally I'd say I was underwhelmed by the food. It was good- nothing was disappointing but really the only thing that wowed me was the octopus. My friend that did a La carte only seemed to like his dishes more.

Service was incredibly slow at moments also. We wound up at the restaurant for over 2 hours. I'd like to come back again and try more of their a la carte menu but honestly for the price of the meal, I may hesitate to come back and opt for trying a new spot instead.

Nice selection of food and have a good variety. Tried several things including the Brussels sprouts, empanadas, and tacos. The tacos were definitely the star of the show. But also, the portions are quite big and of course excellent for sharing, but you can order less than you would at a usual tapas place. Also got a spicy mocktail which was pleasantly not overly sweet and had a good flavor.

Exquisite dining experience.  The octopus was the best I have ever had.  The wine perfectly complimented it all. The service (Dylan) was beyond compare.  She was so attentive and gracious.  The ambiance was the icing on the cake.

Came here last night somewhat reluctantly, as I think ABC kitchen is vastly over rated (partially because the service can be so terrible there). I am really glad I came as I thought ABC Cocina was amazing. We did the pre fixe menu which came with chips and guacamole, shrimp, tuna crudo, mushrooms, fish tacos, a chicken and rice dish and desert. It was honestly way too much food but it was a great experiences

I've had a few friends try both abc kitchen and abc cocina and everyone always said they preferred abc cocina, so I thought I'd give it a try. I liked that the dishes were all tapas style so my friend and I got to try a lot from the menu and they had an extensive drinks menu. We ordered 6 dishes for the 2 of us and I felt like that was the perfect amount of food. 

Highly recommend, would order again:
- guac and chips (honestly this surprised me because it's just guac and chips, but the chips were delicious on their own and the guac had a nice kick to it)
- shrimp was most likely my favorite dish
- calamari texture and seasoning was really good

Fine, not great:
- Maitake mushrooms were a bit bland for me
- pork tacos were good but didn't blow me away
- salad with apple and some kind of cheese was a pass for me 

Our server was excellent - checked in on us periodically and made sure we had everything we needed but did not rush us by any means. We had a 6pm reservation and the place was almost completely empty when we first arrived, but the restaurant was completely packed when we were leaving when it was almost 8pm. Even though there were a lot of people as the night progressed, it didn't feel cramped or uncomfortable. Highly recommend and would come again, especially to try that octopus!
Terribly overpriced. I paid $25 for two small tacos that seemed more like apps to me and I was still hungry afterwards

My girlfriend and I stopped by ABC Cocina for pre-dinner tapas and drinks. We were able to get seated right away at about 6:30pm on a Saturday. After discovering the beers were $15 (wtf?) I ordered the pineapple cocktail which was very good. We got the spicy beef empanadas and the apple, hickory gorgonzola salad. The empanadas were fine and the salad was a bit advanced for our liking. Our server was also a bit short/rude. I think he was upset we only ordered two dishes rather than his recommended two-to-three per person. I'm not sure if they forgot to charge us or if the sparkling water was free but that was a positive. Overall, a decent experience but with some small changes the experience could've been improved significantly.

Service at our table was not very welcoming or excited that we only ordered 2 tapas dishes. 

My boyfriend and I got the apple and hickory salad and for some reason it just felt overly seasoned + with large chunks of salt or something was off. Not used to this taste. We got the beef empanadas which were OK, nothing extremely special.

Overall, I can see how one would feel incentivized to come here because of the ambiance inside, but I think that it is a bit overpriced (beer is $15 and the tapas are a bit expensive too for what it is) and I'm not rushing to come back, unfortunately.

Went there on Sun evening (04.09). Very beautiful ambience. Decor is stunning. Food was great too! We loved guacamole, shrimp with chili oil and flounder tacos. Our waitress was very nice and attentive

We got there a little early for our reservation and had some great drinks at the bar why we were waiting which was a good start. We had a large group for dinner so we ordered a lot of different plates so that we could try a lot of things.  Starting off everything came out really quickly, but the what they started with was more what i would consider more mains. We had ordered the guac and some salads but those did not come our first. We then were sitting around waiting for another 4 dishes we had ordered that for probably around 20 min, we asked our waiter about them and then 2 came out and had to ask the remaining 2 about 15 min later, The weird thing is it was the simple/starter dishes (guac and salads) that were so delayed. It was clear that they had forgotten about us or there had been some kind of error. Besides the service though i would say the food is ok but overpriced for what it is.

We got 6 dishes for 3 people, which was an OK amount of food. We got the ham and cheese fritters, ground beef empanadas, patatas bravas, charred octopus, maitake mushrooms, and chicken tacos. I liked the charred octopus the most. The food was decent, but didn't blow me away for the price. The tacos were my least favorite of the items we ordered. Drinks were good, but our service wasn't great...our waiter was nice, but seemed super busy and it was hard to get his attention to get more drinks. The restaurant was also packed and made me feel kind of claustrophobic. I'd maybe come back again, but wouldn't be the one to suggest it.

Came here for dinner on a Wednesday and we were recommended to order 6 dishes since there were three of us. We got the organic arroz con pollo, spring pea empanadas, crispy calamari, hopper shrimp, charred octopus, and crispy gulf flounder tacos. The spring pea empanadas were surprisingly good. It's got a slight kick to them which made the empanadas really tasty. The portions could be slightly bigger considering how high they are priced. The downside is definitely the service. We felt like we were getting kicked out the moment we were about to finish our food because different staffs would come up to us to ask if they can take away the dishes even though we are clearly still working on them. This happened at least three times and at the end, they did the same thing again by repeatedly asking us if there's anything else they can get for us. This definitely made our dinner less enjoyable and created an unwelcoming environment as we are practically ushered to leave the moment we are finished with a majority of our food...

This place is quite the scene and pricey for what it is. Very loud and dark. The gridled fish tacos were delicious but small and at just two tacos, not worth the $28 price (it also took very long to cook, and my friends were done eating their mains when the fish finally came out). Our server disappeared for about 20 min after we got the check. Another staff member ended up taking our payment. Just very slow service and overpriced for the food.
